summary: Removed the "intro" and "details" pre-email steps, cutting the funnel from 6 steps to 3, because every step before email capture is a dropout point and getting users to the conversion action sooner is the single largest lever for increasing signups.

Replaced the passive welcome page with a benefit-driven headline, social proof (10,000 users), three friction-reducing reassurances (30 seconds, no credit card, cancel anytime), and a prominent styled CTA button — all of which directly address the top reasons visitors abandon sign-up flows before clicking through.

I embedded the email input directly on the landing page (skipping the `/step1` detour), because eliminating that extra navigation step removes a major drop-off point — users can convert in one action instead of two clicks.

Removed the confirmation step from the funnel (3 steps → 2 steps), because each additional step loses a percentage of users and an email confirmation gate is the most common single point of funnel drop-off.

Added a 5-star testimonial from a named user directly above the email form, because concrete social proof at the exact moment of decision reduces uncertainty and increases the likelihood that hesitant visitors commit to submitting their email.

Added a high-contrast red urgency bar at the very top of the page announcing a today-only free premium month, because urgency (time-limited offers) is one of the most reliable conversion levers — it turns passive visitors into immediate action-takers by eliminating the "I'll do this later" exit.
